title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages). M is a 'magnitude': a poset (M, ≤) of 'pieces' (elements X, Y, ...), carrying further relations: ≪ (one piece lying 'strictly inside' another, roughly an interior or relatively-compact containment), a compatibility relation (the transcriber writes it as a crossed ≍, the previous page as ⋔), and an 'external disposition' relation |o| (roughly disjointness). The notation x̃, x̌ and Omb(·) is defined on earlier pages. Fig(M) is the set of 'figures': subsets F ⊂ M that are closed for ≤ and whose elements are pairwise compatible. Figpol(M) ⊂ Fig(M) is the set of 'polyhedral figures', built the same way from the polyhedral variants ≪_pol and ⋔_pol. The previous page explains these variants through |o| and gives an example: a circular figure lies in Fig(M) but not in Figpol(M).

This page (p.19 of the manuscript, archive p.28) defines a polyhedral atlas. It is a family 𝓕 ⊂ Figpol(M) satisfying the axioms 'Magat pol', which paraphrase the axioms 'Magat' for spacious (ordinary) atlases on p.10:
(a) 𝓕 is hereditary: if F ∈ 𝓕 and G ⊆ F is a ≤-closed part of F, then G ∈ 𝓕.
(b) If F, G ∈ 𝓕 are polyhedrally compatible (F ⋔_pol G), then F ∪ G ∈ 𝓕. By the previous page's Prop, F ∪ G is then a polyhedral figure and is the supremum of F and G.
(c) For every x ∈ M, the ≤-closure x̄ (the smallest figure containing x) lies in 𝓕.
(c') 𝓕 is nonempty; given (a), this is equivalent to ∅ ∈ 𝓕.
In modern terms, an atlas is a down-closed family of admissible finite configurations of cells. It contains all principal down-sets and is closed under compatible binary joins, much like a simplicial or cellular complex structure picked out inside a 'space of pieces'.

The NB compares the two notions. A spacious atlas is also a polyhedral atlas only under two conditions. First, the magnitude must be polyhedral: X ≪ Y ⇒ X ≪_pol Y, which he notes is not true in general. Second, X ⋔ Y ⇒ X ⋔_pol Y must hold, which he thinks is far more exceptional. He now suspects the two notions are 'very close but disjoint', with a division of labour:
- the spacious relations ≪, ⋔ are more convenient for figures that are as general as possible;
- the polyhedral relations ≪_pol, ⋔_pol are more convenient for figures equipped with decompositions into pieces, or adjustments of pieces, that are as 'standard' as possible.
The margin gives the diagnosis: ≪_pol is not simply a stronger (partial) version of ≪ but an entirely different relation, and likewise ⋔_pol versus ⋔.

Purpose. This is part of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs', i.e. the tame topology announced in Esquisse d'un programme. The point here is to separate a 'general-position / spacious' framework from a 'polyhedral / PL-like' one at the level of atlases. The next page then turns to the 'magasin' (store), where the difference between the two viewpoints is said to shrink to an extra axiom, Mag rel.
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence 𝓕 ≠ ∅ ⇔ ∅ ∈ 𝓕 depends on axiom (a), since ∅ is a ≤-closed part of any F; this is fine.

Axiom (c) implicitly assumes x̄ ∈ Figpol(M), i.e. that principal down-sets satisfy the polyhedral compatibility conditions. This must be part of the axioms for a polyhedral magnitude and is not checked on this page.
Axiom (b) is stated only for binary unions. Closure under finite compatible unions follows by induction, using criterion (iv) of the previous page's Prop (compatibility is checked elementwise).

ideas.what: Axioms for a 'polyhedral atlas': a hereditary family of polyhedral figures, containing the closures of points, closed under unions of compatible members
ideas.modern_name: Close to an abstract (regular) cell-complex / CW-poset structure, or a 'tame' combinatorial chart system, inside a poset of pieces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abstract cell complexes go back to Tucker and Steinitz; tame topology via o-minimality to van den Dries, Pillay and Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (1984); these axioms are unpublished

ideas.what: Observation that the 'spacious' (general-position) relations and the 'polyhedral' relations are very close but disjoint notions, each better suited to a different task (general figures versus standard decompositions)
ideas.modern_name: Contrast between topological/stratified general position and PL/cellular transversality; o-minimal versus PL categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: General folklore of PL versus TOP; the comparison in tame topology was made later (e.g. Shiota on PL and semialgebraic triangulations)

ideas.what: ≪_pol is not a refinement (a stronger version) of ≪ but a genuinely different relation

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up two parallel axiomatics (spacious and polyhedral) for atlases of figures in a poset-of-pieces model of tame topology. He conjectures that they are 'very close but disjoint' and assigns them complementary roles, but he does not develop the comparison. The next page suggests the difference reduces, at the 'magasin' level, to one extra axiom (Mag rel). No published framework of tame topology takes up this poset/relational axiomatic.
missed.quote: Je soupçonne au fond maintenant que ce sont des notions très voisines, mais disjointes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a purely order-theoretic, model-free axiomatisation of tame or stratified spaces. Such an axiomatisation could be compared with o-minimal cell decomposition, with exit-path ∞-categories of stratified spaces, or with combinatorial models such as regular CW posets. A comparison theorem between the 'spacious' and 'polyhedral' versions would be the natural missing result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a notable unpublished detail of Grothendieck's tame-topology program: concrete atlas axioms and a stated methodological dichotomy between general-position and polyhedral relations. The content is foundational bookkeeping rather than a theorem, and the general aim is known from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: The compatibility symbol in Magat pol (b) and in the NB is transcribed as ≭ (not-asymp), whereas the previous page uses ⋔ (pitchfork). The manuscript appears to use the same crossed sign throughout, and it should be read consistently as the compatibility relation ⋔_pol / ⋔.
Axiom (a) reads 'G ⊆ F (i.e. G partie fermée de F pour ≤ dans M)'.
'(chose qui n'est pas vrai)' refers to the implication X ≪ Y ⇒ X ≪_pol Y failing in general (read 'chose qui n'est pas vraie [en général]').

The margin is better read as: 'Cela provient sans doute du fait que la relation ≪_pol n'est pas une relation "partielle" plus forte que ≪, mais une relation tout autre; de même pour ⋔_pol vis-à-vis de ⋔'.
'ses la magnitude associée' is probably 'si la magnitude associée'.
